corrections.claim: Cook in 1971 and Levin in 1973 showed SAT is NP-complete; Karp in 1972 reduced 21 classic problems to it, and relativizing proofs cannot settle P versus NP.
corrections.problem: The reduction runs the wrong way. Reducing problems TO SAT only shows they are in NP. Karp showed hardness by reducing SAT (through chains of reductions) to each of his 21 problems, and SAT is itself one of the 21.
corrections.correct: Karp in 1972 showed 21 classic problems NP-complete, including SAT itself, through chains of polynomial-time reductions from SAT.
corrections.evidence: Karp 1972, Reducibility Among Combinatorial Problems: the reduction tree is rooted at SATISFIABILITY and runs outward to clique, vertex cover, Hamiltonian circuit, and so on.

corrections.claim: the square root of the absolute value of xy satisfies them at the origin and has none [source: src_formal_gray_morris_1978]; emit: 'Gray and Morris give the counterexample that the raw cache missed'
corrections.problem: The sqrt|xy| counterexample is the classic one from Titchmarsh (1939), not from Gray and Morris. The Gray and Morris (AMM 1978) example is exp(-z^-4) with f(0)=0, which satisfies Cauchy-Riemann everywhere but is not continuous at 0.
corrections.correct: Cite Titchmarsh, The Theory of Functions (2nd ed., 1939) for sqrt|xy|, or keep Gray and Morris but use their exp(-z^-4) example. Fix the emit ~#proof line to match.
corrections.evidence: The Wikipedia Cauchy-Riemann equations article (fetched 2026-10-02) cites Titchmarsh 1939 for sqrt|xy| and Gray and Morris 1978 for exp(-z^-4).

corrections.claim: Wigner called the fit ... unreasonable; the examples include Riemannian geometry in general relativity and Hilbert spaces in quantum mechanics.
corrections.problem: Riemannian geometry in general relativity is not one of Wigner's examples. His three worked examples are Newton's law of gravitation and planetary motion, matrix mechanics and the helium ground state, and the Lamb shift in QED. He discusses the complex Hilbert space of quantum mechanics as a striking case. He names 'four dimensional Riemann space' only when contrasting relativity with quantum theory as possibly ununifiable, not as evidence of effectiveness.
corrections.correct: Wigner's examples include Newton's gravitation, matrix mechanics with the helium spectrum, and the Lamb shift, and he singles out the complex Hilbert space of quantum mechanics. Riemannian geometry in GR is a later commentators' example, not Wigner's.
corrections.evidence: Full text of Wigner 1960 (CPAM 13(1)), fetched from webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/wigner.pdf on 2026-10-02.

corrections.claim: example: Raft keeps at most one leader per term even when messages are lost or delayed, and makes progress while a majority of servers can talk; source: src_formal_lynch_1996
corrections.problem: Raft dates from 2014 (Ongaro and Ousterhout), so Lynch's 1996 textbook cannot be its source. The liveness half also leaves out Raft's timing assumption: progress needs election timeouts well above broadcast time, not only a connected majority. Leaving it out undercuts the gloss's own point that guarantees depend on the fault model.
corrections.correct: Cite src_formal_ongaro_ousterhout_2014 for the Raft example. State progress as 'makes progress while a majority can communicate within the election-timeout bound'.
corrections.evidence: src_formal_ongaro_ousterhout_2014 already exists in registries/sources/formal.spw; Raft paper section 5.6 on timing and availability.

corrections.claim: Hindley in 1969 and Milner in 1978 gave principal types for let-polymorphism
corrections.problem: Hindley 1969 proved principal type-schemes for terms of combinatory logic, which has no let construct. Let-polymorphism is Milner's 1978 contribution.
corrections.correct: Hindley in 1969 proved principal type-schemes for combinatory logic; Milner in 1978 independently gave principal types with let-polymorphism for ML; Damas and Milner proved Algorithm W complete in 1982.
corrections.evidence: Title of Hindley 1969: 'The Principal Type-Scheme of an Object in Combinatory Logic' (Trans. AMS 146).

corrections.claim: Church and Turing showed independently in 1936 that no algorithm decides first-order validity [source: src_formal_church_1936 = 'An Unsolvable Problem of Elementary Number Theory', AJM 58(2)]
corrections.problem: The AJM paper proves that lambda-definability and normal form are undecidable. Church's undecidability of first-order validity is in 'A Note on the Entscheidungsproblem', JSL 1(1):40-41, 1936. Equivalence of lambda calculus and Turing machines was proved by Turing in 1937, 'Computability and lambda-definability', JSL 2.
corrections.correct: Add src_formal_church_1936b, A Note on the Entscheidungsproblem, JSL 1(1), 1936, for the validity claim. Attribute the equivalence to Turing 1937.

corrections.claim: Fourier introduced trigonometric series to solve heat conduction in his 1822 Theorie analytique de la chaleur, the root of separation of variables.
corrections.problem: Fourier did not introduce trigonometric series. D. Bernoulli, Euler, and d'Alembert used them and separated variables for the vibrating string in the 1740s and 1750s. Fourier's heat work dates from the 1807 memoir. His contribution was claiming that arbitrary functions expand in such series and applying them systematically to heat.
corrections.correct: Fourier, in work begun with his 1807 memoir and published as the 1822 Theorie analytique de la chaleur, claimed that arbitrary functions have trigonometric series and used them with separation of variables to solve heat conduction; both tools had earlier uses by Bernoulli and Euler.

corrections.claim: With unsigned messages, agreement despite f Byzantine replicas needs at least 3f plus 1 replicas, and PBFT reaches that bound under partial synchrony.
corrections.problem: The 'unsigned messages' qualifier applies only to the synchronous Lamport-Shostak-Pease bound. Under partial synchrony, where PBFT runs, n >= 3f+1 is required even with unforgeable signatures (Dwork, Lynch, Stockmeyer 1988). Read together, the claim and its limits suggest signatures could lower PBFT's replica count. The registry cell formal.consensus.bft_replicas_f1 has the same framing.
corrections.correct: In synchronous systems with oral (unsigned) messages, Byzantine agreement needs 3f+1 replicas (LSP 1982). Under partial synchrony, 3f+1 is needed even with signatures (DLS 1988), and PBFT meets that bound.
corrections.evidence: src_formal_dls_1988 is already in the registry.

corrections.claim: provenance correction: 'Lean 4 is no longer said to run the Calculus of Inductive Constructions; it uses its own dependent type theory with inductive types'

corrections.correct: Lean 4 uses a variant of the Calculus of Inductive Constructions (CoC with non-cumulative universes, inductive types, definitional proof irrelevance, and quotients); it is a separate prover with a separate kernel from Rocq.
corrections.evidence: lean-lang.org Theorem Proving in Lean 4, Dependent Type Theory chapter, fetched 2026-10-02.

corrections.claim: for p equal to 1 this needs a sigma-finite measure (also in emit: 'the dual of L1 ... need sigma-finite measures')
corrections.problem: Sigma-finiteness is sufficient for (L1)* = L-infinity, not necessary. The identity holds for wider classes such as localizable (decomposable) measures. 'Needs' states a sufficient hypothesis as a necessary one, which is the reverse of the hypothesis-drop this ledger guards against.
corrections.correct: For p = 1, (L1)* = L-infinity holds when the measure is sigma-finite, and more generally for localizable measures; it can fail for some non-sigma-finite measures.
corrections.evidence: Folland 1999, Theorem 6.15 states sigma-finite as a sufficient condition; Exercise 6.23 discusses semifinite and decomposable cases.

corrections.claim: limits.fails: a real rotation by 90 degrees has no real eigenvalues and no real Jordan form; rational canonical form covers that case
corrections.problem: A real Jordan form (real canonical form) does exist, with 2-by-2 rotation-scaling blocks for complex-conjugate eigenvalue pairs. What fails is the complex Jordan form over the reals.
corrections.correct: A real rotation by 90 degrees has no real eigenvalues, so it has no Jordan form over the reals; the real Jordan form with 2-by-2 blocks, or the rational canonical form, covers that case.

corrections.problem: A fresh alkaline AA has about 0.1-0.3 ohm internal resistance, far below the smallest load. Power therefore rises steadily toward the 2 ohm resistor, and the experiment never shows a peak at the matched load, so it cannot demonstrate the claim it points to. Its own numbers are also unsafe: about 1.5-1.6 V across 2 ohms is about 1.1 W, more than twice a 0.5 W rating.
corrections.correct: Use a source whose internal resistance falls inside the load sweep, such as a 9 V battery or a cell with an added series resistor (for example 4.7 ohm), sweep loads on both sides of it, and size each resistor for at least V^2/R with margin (1-2 W for the low values). Alternatively, retarget the try to measuring internal resistance only, not finding the power peak.

The domains are homologous; only the assembly of the NB-LRR architecture is argued to be independent. #!settled and #!refuted are stronger than the evidence supports.

corrections.claim: The word doula, Greek for servant-woman, entered anthropology by 1972; Dana Raphael used it in 1973 for women who support new mothers.
corrections.problem: This makes Raphael look like a later adopter. Raphael introduced the term: Wikipedia says it was 'first used in English in a 1969 anthropological study conducted by Dana Raphael'. Her 1973 book popularized it. Etymonline's 'by 1972' is only a latest-by date and does not name a different coiner.

The labor-support sense came from Klaus and Kennell, visible in Sosa et al. 1980, and DONA was founded in 1992. Raphael is also wrongly placed after the coinage instead of as its source.

corrections.claim: register broader: variable (and variable narrower: register)
corrections.problem: This is a category error in the lattice. A sociolinguistic variable is a set of alternative variants, for example postvocalic r. A register is a variety defined by its situation of use. A register is not a kind of variable. Registers are marked by co-occurring variants, and variables shift by register, but neither is a narrower term of the other.
corrections.correct: Link register to variable with 'see' or 'related' (variables shift across registers), not broader/narrower. If a broader term is wanted, use a 'variety' node above both dialect and register.

corrections.claim: Ladder rung '2019 and 2020 citations: moderator of a forum, streamer to a live audience' (and moderator rung '2019 citation: enforcer of a discussion forum')

Moderated Usenet groups and mailing lists had moderators decades earlier, and live-stream 'streamers' were common by the early 2010s. corrections.claim: The claim that reminders of money make people more self-reliant and less helpful failed preregistered replications... counter: Klein 2014, Rohrer, Pashler and Harris 2015, Vadillo 2016, Lodder 2019
corrections.problem: The cited replications do not test the claim as stated. Many Labs 1 (Klein 2014) and Rohrer, Pashler and Harris 2015 replicated Caruso et al. 2013, where a money prime was said to raise system justification and free-market views. They did not replicate Vohs, Mead and Goode 2006 on self-sufficiency and helping. Vadillo 2016 is a commentary on selection bias. Only the Lodder 2019 meta-analysis supports the broad null: preregistered studies show roughly zero effect, plus strong signs of publication bias. Calling the claim '#!refuted' through these citations pins the wrong failed replications on the Vohs claim.
corrections.correct: State that money-priming effects, including Caruso et al.'s system-justification effect (failed in Many Labs 1 and in Rohrer et al. 2015), did not survive preregistered tests. Cite Lodder et al. 2019 for 'no evidence in preregistered studies'. Either drop the specific 'self-reliant and less helpful' wording or cite a direct replication of Vohs 2006. Consider marking the claim 'failed replication' rather than refuted.
corrections.evidence: Rohrer et al. 2015 is titled 'Do Subtle Reminders of Money Change People's Political Views?' (JEP:G 144(4)). The Many Labs 1 'currency priming' item was Caruso et al. 2013. Lodder et al. 2019 (JEP:G 148(4)) is a meta-analysis that finds a null in preregistered studies.

corrections.claim: Pigou sorted price discrimination into three degrees: a price per unit tuned to each buyer, prices that vary with quantity or version, and prices set by observable group.
corrections.problem: Pigou's second degree is pricing by blocks of quantity: the seller sets a few prices and buyers sort themselves by the amount they buy. 'Version' (versioning or quality menus) is a modern reading from Shapiro and Varian and later screening theory. It is not in Pigou 1920, yet the sentence attributes it to him.

corrections.evidence: Pigou, The Economics of Welfare (1920), Part II ch. XVII. Varian 1989 (already in the registry) separates Pigou's quantity-based second degree from later self-selection or versioning readings.
